sec: Note: the causes of metabolic acidosis revisited · p825

items.q: Match the second branch of metabolic acidosis — 1) Acid generation  2) Alkali loss  3) Alkali loss — GI causes  4) Alkali loss — renal causes … A) NAGMA with positive urine anion gap  B) High anion gap  C) NAGMA with negative urine anion gap  D) VIPoma
items.exp: Note flowchart: acid generation → high anion gap; alkali loss → GI causes (VIPoma) with a negative urine anion gap, versus renal causes (RTA) with a positive urine anion gap. (Book p825)

items.q: In the note flowchart, metabolic acidosis from acid generation carries which anion gap?
opts: High anion gap
Normal anion gap with a negative UAG
Normal anion gap with a positive UAG
A normal anion gap that cannot be calculated
items.exp: Acid generation → high anion gap; alkali loss → NAGMA, further split into GI (−ve UAG) and renal (+ve UAG). (Book p825)

items.q: A patient with a VIPoma has a normal anion gap acidosis. What is the expected urine anion gap, and why?
opts: Negative — GI alkali loss with the kidney responding normally
Positive — GI alkali loss with a tubular defect
Negative — because acid generation raises unmeasured anions
Positive — because VIPoma damages the distal tubule
items.exp: GI causes of NAGMA are marked (−ve) for the urine anion gap, with VIPoma as the printed example; renal causes (RTA) are (+ve). (Book p825)

items.q: ‘In the p825 note, both GI and renal causes of NAGMA are marked with a positive urine anion gap.’
opts: False — GI causes are (−ve) and renal causes are (+ve) for the urine anion gap
True — the positive mark applies to both columns
False — both columns are marked negative
False — urine anion gap is marked only for the acid-generation branch
items.exp: The note marks GI causes NAGMA (−ve) with VIPoma as the example, and renal causes NAGMA (+ve) with RTA as the example. (Book p825)

items.q: All but one of these statements match the p825 note. Which is the odd one out?
opts: RTA is the example of alkali loss with a negative urine anion gap
High anion gap acidosis belongs to the acid-generation branch
VIPoma is the example of a GI cause of NAGMA
Alkali loss splits into GI and renal columns
items.exp: RTA is the *positive* urine anion gap example under renal alkali loss; the negative marking belongs to the GI column, whose example is VIPoma. (Book p825)
